newsitem.title: INDIA: India Congress withdraws support to government.
newsitem.headline: India Congress withdraws support to government.

text.p: India's Congress party on Sunday withdrew support for Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda, throwing the survival of the fragile ruling coalition into doubt.
Sitaram Kesri, president of the Congress, met President Shankar Dayal Sharma at noon (0630 GMT) and handed over a letter announcing the decision.

Asked to confirm a news agency report that the Congress had decided to withdraw support to Deve Gowda's nine-month-old government, Kesri told Reuters: "Yes. It has been done." He refused to elaborate.
It was not immediately clear if the Congress decision meant Deve Gowda would have to resign and call a mid-term election.

Agriculture Minister Chaturanan Mishra, a communist member of the government, told Reuters he felt Deve Gowda should resign. "The government was dependent on the Congress party's support and if that support is withdrawn it is logical that the government should resign."
A Congress spokesman said the party had called a news conference at 4:00 p.m. (1030 GMT), after an emergency meeting of the Congress Working Committee, the party's policy-making body.
Congress officials said the withdrawal decision followed "attempts by the United Front" to split the Congress party in the key north Indian state of Uttar Pradesh.

The rightwing Hindu Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) formed a coalition government in the state earlier this month, thwarting Congress attempts to rule the politically crucial region which sends 85 deputies to the 545-member Lok Sabha or lower house of parliament.
BJP leader Atal Behari Vajpayee was quoted by the Press Trust of India news agency as saying the Congress withdrawal of support would inevitably lead to a mid-term election.
Deve Gowda's minority 15-member United Front alliance which groups free-traders, communists and centrists, controls some 178 deputies in the Lok Sabha. The Congress has 142 deputies.
Kamaluddin Ahmed, a Congress leader, when asked if the party's withdrawal of support meant a snap mid-term national election, told Reuters: "Don't be silly. We will form our own government."
Government officials were not immediately available for comment. The United Front office, a stone's throw from the Congress party office in New Delhi, wore a deserted look.
The Congress supported the government but was not part of the ruling alliance and holds no cabinet posts.
